title.rendered: ⚠️ Security Notice: Phishing Scam Targeting DH2026 Participants

content.rendered:
We have received reports that fraudulent (“phishing”) emails impersonating DH2026 and its organizers are being sent to conference participants. These messages falsely claim to handle hotel reservations and travel arrangements for the conference and attempt to collect personal information and payment.

Example of a known fraudulent message

  • Sender: ops@gtravelservice.com (posing as “OPS GTE”)
  • Subject: “Reservation Confirmation in Daejeon, South Korea – July 27–31, 2026 – Daejeon Convention Center”
  • Content: Requests hotel-booking details, travel information, and payment

The senders appear to harvest presenters’ email addresses from public conference pages and published abstracts, then send unsolicited “reservation” emails at random. This is a common form of academic-conference fraud, sometimes called a “housing pirate” scam.

Please remember:

  • For accommodation, DH2026 works only with officially designated booking partners, which are listed on our official hotel reservation page.
  • We will never ask you to provide credit-card details, make payments, or submit personal travel information through unsolicited emails or external links.
  • Any official information about accommodation, registration, and payment is published only on our official website and sent only from our official account.

Official DH2026 channels:

  • Website: https://dh2026.adho.org
  • Email: kadh2026@gmail.com
  • Registration: ConfTool (https://www.conftool.pro/dh2026)
  • Event app: Whova

If you receive a suspicious email:

  1. Do not reply, click any links, or open attachments.
  2. Do not provide any personal or payment information.
  3. Delete the message or mark it as spam.
  4. If possible, forward it to kadh2026@gmail.com so we can warn other participants.

If you are unsure whether a message is genuine, please contact us at kadh2026@gmail.com before taking any action. We are grateful to the participants who alerted us to this scam.

title.rendered: DH2026 Main Conference Program Now Available

content.rendered:
We are pleased to announce that the Main Conference Program for DH2026 (Daejeon, Republic of Korea) is now available.

View the program

  • Online program (live & searchable): https://dh2026.adho.org/program-agenda/
  • Printable PDF: https://dh2026.adho.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/DH2026_Main_Conference_Program.pdf

The online version is interactive — you can filter by day, track, and paper type, and search by title, author, or affiliation to locate your presentation and see exactly when and where it takes place. It always reflects the most current schedule.

At a glance

  • Pre-conference events: Monday–Tuesday, July 27–28
  • Opening Ceremony, Opening Keynote (Prof. Kim Hyeon) & Reception: Tuesday, July 28, 18:00
  • Main conference: Wednesday–Friday, July 29–31 — 111 parallel sessions across 11 tracks · 421 presentations · 94 posters on display throughout the conference
  • Three keynotes (Grand Ballroom): Prof. Kim Hyeon (Opening), Prof. Maciej Eder (Antonio Zampolli Prize Lecture, Wed 10:30), and Prof. Kirsten Thorpe (Closing, Fri 16:00)

For presenting authors Please check the day, time, track, and presentation format of your contribution. If you notice any error, or your circumstances have changed (e.g., switching to virtual presentation, or withdrawal), contact us at kadh2026@gmail.com as soon as possible. Note that at least one author of each accepted submission must be registered for the presentation to remain in the program.

Registration: https://dh2026.adho.org/conference-registration/ (via ConfTool: https://www.conftool.pro/dh2026)

Room assignments and session chairs will be announced closer to the conference. Questions? Write to us at kadh2026@gmail.com.

We look forward to welcoming you to Daejeon this July.

— On behalf of the DH2026 Program Committee and Local Organizing Committee

title.rendered: AVinDH Mini-Conference at DH2026: 10 Years of AudioVisual & Digital Humanities

content.rendered:
The AudioVisual & Digital Humanities Special Interest Group (AVinDH SIG) will hold its 10th-anniversary mini-conference at DH2026 in Daejeon, South Korea. The full-day session invites all DH2026 attendees to reflect on a decade of work on audiovisual materials in the Digital Humanities and to shape the future of the community.

Programme Highlights

  • Welcome & Introduction
  • Panel: “AVinDH SIG turns 10!” — reflections on past, present, and future, with discussants Lauren Tilton (University of Richmond) and Michaël Bourgatte (Université de Lorraine), moderated by Alison Langmead (University of Pittsburgh)
  • Speed Dating — a structured networking activity
  • Lightning Talks — 5-minute presentations on current AVinDH research
  • Tool Cavalcade — 5-minute showcases of AVinDH tools
  • Wrap-up — final reflections on future directions

Participation

📅 Date: Monday, July 27, 2026 🤝 Format: In-Person + Virtual (with AI translation support) 📝 Registration: Open to all DH2026 attendees — you do not need to be a member of the AVinDH SIG to participate.

🔗 Workshop page & registration form 🔗 Browse all DH2026 pre-conference events

For questions, please contact Mila Oiva at mila.oiva@fau.de.

title.rendered: Call for Abstracts: Distant Past(s) – Current Future(s) — Mini-Conference at DH2026

content.rendered:
The organizing committee of the mini-conference “Distant Past(s) – Current Future(s): Digitization, Digital Objects and Datafication Approaches in Ancient and Medieval Studies” is now accepting submissions for DH2026.

About the Mini-Conference

This full-day mini-conference on Tuesday, July 28, 2026 offers an exchange platform for ancient civilizations and medieval studies scholars venturing into DH practices and tools, those with experience bridging historical evidence and technical approaches, and technical experts contributing to ancient and medieval projects. Submissions are welcome on topics including ethics, accessibility, reuse, mapping, ownership, imaging, engagement, curation, and more.

Submission Details

  • Deadline: May 1, 2026 (23:59 UTC+1)
  • Abstract length: 250–300 words
  • Submission: Via online form only
  • Formats: Long Talk (20 min) or Short Talk (10 min)

Scholars and practitioners at all career stages are welcome, and Early Career Researchers (ECRs) are strongly encouraged to submit. This CFP is open to all researchers — you do not need to have an accepted submission in the main DH2026 program to apply. Selected contributors will need to register for DH2026.

For full details, visit the mini-conference page: https://vlandau.notion.site/distant-pasts-current-futures-2026

Browse all pre-conference events: https://dh2026.adho.org/pre-conference-events/

title.rendered: Call for Papers: Playing Heaven – Remapping Early Modern Neo-Confucian Worlds with AI

content.rendered:
The “Playing Heaven” team is now accepting paper submissions for their mini-conference at DH2026, scheduled for 28 July 2026 (Pre-Conference Day 2).

This mini-conference invites intellectual historians, specialists in early modern East Asia, and scholars in the digital humanities to present 20-minute papers on the effective application of artificial intelligence to the study of the history of ideas, cultural history, and multilingual historical research.

About the Project

“Playing Heaven” is an inter-university collaboration based in Hong Kong and Singapore and one of the inaugural recipients of the Schmidt Sciences Humanities and AI Virtual Institute (HAVI) grant. The project seeks to rethink the intellectual and cultural history of early modern East Asia through the development of a domain-specific AI system. Rather than treating philosophical schools, literary traditions, and cultural practices as fixed categories, the project approaches them as historically contingent formations shaped by processes of transmission, adaptation, and reinterpretation.

This DH2026 mini-conference constitutes the second part of the Playing Heaven team’s project launch. The first launch event is scheduled to be held at the University of Hong Kong on 1 June 2026.

Submission Guidelines

DH2026 Playing Heaven CFPDownload
  • Abstract length: Up to 500 words in English (excluding bibliography)
  • Format: PDF
  • Submission deadline: 21 April 2026, 23:59 (anywhere on Earth)
  • Submit to: javiercha@hku.hk
  • Notification of acceptance: 30 April 2026

Submissions will be evaluated on the basis of originality, rigour, and significance. Selected contributors will be required to register for DH2026.

For further information, please contact Javier Cha (javiercha@hku.hk).

title.rendered: Call for Papers: ICLA DCL / SIG-DLS Mini-Conference — “Digital and/or Comparative Literary Studies Today”

content.rendered:
We are pleased to announce the Call for Papers for a mini-conference titled “Digital and/or Comparative Literary Studies Today”, jointly organized by the ICLA Digital Comparative Literature (DCL) research committee and ADHO’s Special Interest Group in Digital Literary Studies (SIG-DLS), taking place as part of DH2026 in Daejeon, South Korea (July 27–31, 2026).

Following the success of their event at DH2025 Lisbon, this half-day mini-conference explores the intersection of digital/computational and comparative approaches to literary studies — from distant reading, cultural analytics, and network analysis to generative AI and born-digital literature. Contributions addressing multilingual, cross-cultural, and interdisciplinary research are particularly welcome.

The mini-conference consists of two parts: a lightning talks session followed by an interactive poster session. Free on-site poster printing is expected to be available for most participants.

Key Dates

  • Submission deadline: April 30, 2026
  • Notification of acceptance: May 21, 2026
  • Mini-conference date: July 28, 2026 (afternoon, KST)

Submission Guidelines 300–500 word abstracts (excluding references) in PDF format, submitted to Christof Schöch at schoech@uni-trier.de.

For full details, visit: 🔗 https://icla-dcl.quarto.pub/info/news/2026/dh-mini-conference.html

For inquiries, please contact Simone Rebora at simone.rebora@univr.it.

title.rendered: Call for Papers: AI4AS 2026 — AI for Ancient Studies Mini-Conference at DH2026

content.rendered:
We are pleased to announce the Call for Papers for AI4AS 2026 (AI for Ancient Studies), a mini-conference taking place as part of DH2026 in Daejeon, South Korea (July 27–31, 2026).

AI4AS 2026 focuses on engagement and fragility, critically examining the opportunities and risks that generative AI introduces into the study, interpretation, and dissemination of ancient non-alphabetic languages. The mini-conference gathers experts across diverse ancient-language traditions to build a shared understanding of responsible AI adoption within Ancient World Studies.

Key Dates

  • Submission deadline: April 7 17, 2026 (11:59 pm AoE)
  • Notification of acceptance: April 15 24, 2026
  • Camera-ready abstract due: April 20 28, 2026

Submission Guidelines Abstracts of max 500 words in English, submitted as PDF to ai4asconference@gmail.com with [AI4AS2026] in the subject line.

For full details, visit the AI4AS 2026 CFP page: 🔗 https://ai4asconference.github.io/2026/call-for-papers.html

Selected contributors will be required to register for DH2026 via ConfTool. Early bird registration is available until May 18, 2026.

For questions, please contact the AI4AS Organizing Committee:

  • Chiara Salvador, University of Montpellier Paul-Valéry
  • Angelica Lo Duca, National Research Council (CNR), Italy

title.rendered: Review Assignments for DH2026 Have Been Sent

content.rendered:
We are pleased to announce that review assignments for the Digital Humanities Conference 2026 (DH2026) have been distributed to all reviewers.

Check Your Inbox

If you have registered as a reviewer, you should have received an email with details about your assigned submissions. Please check your inbox, including your spam or junk folder.

Didn’t receive an email? No worries! You can still access your review assignments by logging in to ConfTool directly:

🔗 Access Your Review Assignments

Review Deadline

Please complete all assigned reviews by January 20, 2026. Your timely completion is crucial for keeping the overall conference schedule on track.

Review Criteria and Assessment Categories

Reviews should be conducted in accordance with ADHO’s established review criteria, as outlined in the CFP and related ADHO documentation.

In the submission system, you will see five assessment categories:

  • Evaluation (20%) – Does the submission provide a sufficient description of the current state of knowledge and best practices relevant to the work, supported by appropriate references?
  • Significance (20%) – Does the work go beyond the current state of knowledge and best practices in its field(s), whether in method, approach, application domain, or findings?
  • Methodology (20%) – Does the submission describe its approach or method with enough detail for readers to understand what was done and why, within the limits of the abstract format?
  • Diversity (15%) – Does the submission contribute to diversity by expanding the range of topics, approaches, or perspectives represented at the conference, and/or by giving appropriate recognition to a broad range of relevant scholarly work?
  • Readability (15%) – Is the submission well structured and clearly written in a way that supports reader comprehension?

Double-Anonymous Review

DH2026 follows the double-anonymous (blind) review principle. Authors’ and reviewers’ identities must not be disclosed, and submissions should be assessed solely on their scholarly merits. Please avoid speculation about authorship and flag any potential identifying information encountered in submissions.

Use of Large Language Models (LLMs)

To protect the confidentiality of the review process, please refrain from entering submission content into any large language model (LLM) or external AI tool. LLMs may be used only for light proofreading or language refinement of your own review texts, on the condition that no data are stored or used for training purposes.

Questions or Conflicts of Interest?

If you need to recuse yourself from any review, please select the “conflict of interest” option in ConfTool, and we will reassign it promptly. For any other questions, feel free to contact us.

Thank you for contributing your time and expertise to DH2026. Your careful and thoughtful reviews play a vital role in shaping a strong and inclusive conference program.

The Program Committee of DH2026 Daejeon

title.rendered: DH2026 Submissions Now Closed: Thank You for 813 Proposals!

content.rendered:
Dear DH Community,
We are pleased to announce that the submission period for DH2026 has now closed. Following the extended deadline of December 15, 2024 (23:59 KST), we received a total of 813 submissions.
We wish to express our sincere gratitude to all who submitted their work. The volume and breadth of proposals reflect the continued vitality of the digital humanities community and the strong interest in convening in South Korea next year.
As the submission system is now closed, we regret that we are unable to accept any further submissions.
The Program Committee will now begin the review process. We will communicate further updates regarding the review timeline and notifications in due course.
Thank you once again for your enthusiasm and support.

title.rendered: Deadline Extension: DH2026 Call for Proposals

content.rendered:

Next year’s conference (July 27–31, 2026) will be hosted by the Korean Association for Digital Humanities (KADH) at the Daejeon Convention Center in Daejeon, South Korea. The theme for this conference is “Engagement.” Submissions are welcome in multiple formats, including long and short papers, posters, panels, workshops, and mini-conferences.

Please visit the Call for Proposals on the conference website for more details: https://dh2026.adho.org/cfp.

We invite you to share your work with the global Digital Humanities community.
